items.title: 警訊浮現！標普500強勢攻高 為什麼近6成成分股悄悄進入熊市？
items.title_en: Alert Signals Appear! S&P 500 Races Higher—Why Nearly 60% of Its Components Have Quietly Slipped Into a Bear Market?
paras: 在科技股及其他人工智慧(AI)概念股帶動下，標普500指數正直逼先前創下的歷史新高，但亮麗的表現背後出現令人擔憂的趨勢：近六成成分股與歷史高點相比跌逾20%——換句話說，參與股市漲勢的股票比例正在縮小。
根據道瓊市場數據，標普500指數周一(21日)收盤距離8月13日創下的歷史收盤高點7798.99點僅差0.4%。與此同時，那斯達克綜合指數同日收盤突破6月初創下的前一波高點27093.90點。

大型科技股領漲 AMD股價飆近10%

經歷一段表現溫吞的行情後，Meta(META-US)在內的「科技七巨頭」(Magnificent Seven)中的大型科技股周一重新扮演重要推手。半導體股、記憶體股及硬體股也大幅走高，超微(AMD-US)股價飆升9.95%。
這波漲勢凸顯企業獲利驚人增長的吸引力，以及未來幾年AI建設可望每年帶來約1兆美元資本支出的龐大投資熱潮。
然而股市表面之下仍存在弱勢，關稅、通膨、能源價格飆升及借貸成本上升，都已對市場造成壓力。
Ameriprise首席市場策略師Anthony Saglimbene說：「市場廣度實際上已經惡化，儘管指數正逐步逼近歷史新高。」他指的是目前參與股市漲勢的股票比例正在縮小。
Saglimbene表示，儘管AI概念股重新受到市場青睞，但公用事業股表現疲弱，非必需消費品類股也面臨壓力，包括汽車零組件、紡織品及精品相關股票，「很多股票都遠低於52周高點。」

標普逼近新高 逾半成分股卻跌逾20%

儘管標普500指數重新逼近8月高點，但根據道瓊市場數據，標普500成分股中有59.2%較歷史高點下跌至少20%。
華爾街許多人將從歷史高點下跌至少20%視為進入熊市的定義。不過，許多重挫的標普500成分股近期波動劇烈，幾個月內就可能出現20%甚至更大的漲跌幅。
根據道瓊市場數據，至少自2017年底以來，標普500指數從未在距離歷史高點不到1%的同時，還有如此高比例的成分股較自己曾創下的歷史高點下跌20%以上。這也是2022年10月這波多頭行情啟動以來，首度出現這種情況。
不過，雖然有些投資人認為這反映市場潛在風險，但也有一派認為這顯示市場仍具韌性。
富蘭克林坦伯頓研究所(Franklin Templeton Institute)資深市場策略師Chris Galipeau表示，一般人可能會認為「事情會開始失控」，例如汽油與柴油價格飆升、伊朗戰爭，以及聯準會(Fed)實現2%通膨目標的公信力遭質疑等問題。
但Galipeau表示，今年前六個月美國經濟與企業獲利的韌性都超出預期，「這個故事很被難反駁」，除非Fed最終大幅升息並拖累經濟成長。

油價與高殖利率仍是市場隱憂

儘管如此，伊朗戰爭、10年期美國公債殖利率接近5%，以及Fed重新強化抗通膨立場，都影響目前投資人的資金配置方向。
美國汽油價格目前每加侖衝上4.50美元，柴油價格也達到創紀錄的每加侖6.50美元，同時生活成本及借貸成本也持續上升。
然而，即使Fed升息一次或數次，預料也不太會阻止超大規模雲端服務商(hyperscalers)繼續為AI大舉投資。
Schwab金融研究中心宏觀經濟研究與策略主管Kevin Gordon說：「這一直是一個大規模的資金輪動過程。但對我而言，這就是今年市場的本質。你會看到某些產業與類股出現一段時間的疲弱，但不會所有產業同時走弱。」
全球基準布蘭特原油價格這三個月來上漲約25%，重新回到每桶100美元，加劇了許多家庭的生活成本危機。
然而，標普500中的許多能源股仍在接近歷史高點的位置交易，包括馬拉松石油(MPC-US)、Valero Energy(VLO-US)及Phillips 66(PSX-US)。這些個股周一都收黑，跌幅在4-5%之間。
Gordon形容，市場目前呈現「謹慎攀越憂慮之牆」的格局。
paras_en: Driven by tech stocks and other artificial‑intelligence (AI) concept shares, the S&P 500 index is closing in on its previous all‑time high, but a worrying trend lurks behind the shine: almost six‑tenths of its components have fallen more than 20% from their historic peaks—meaning the share of stocks participating in the market rally is shrinking.

According to Dow Jones market data, the S&P 500 closed on Monday (the 21st) just 0.4% shy of the August 13 record closing high of 7,798.99 points. At the same time, the Nasdaq Composite also broke through its early‑June peak of 27,093.90 points on the same day.

Large‑cap tech leads the surge – AMD jumps nearly 10% After a period of tepid performance, the “Magnificent Seven” tech giants, including Meta (META‑US), returned to the forefront on Monday. Semiconductor, memory and hardware stocks also rallied sharply, with AMD (AMD‑US) soaring 9.95%.

The rally underscores the appeal of astonishing corporate profit growth and the massive investment wave expected as AI build‑out could drive roughly $1 trillion of capital spending each year over the next few years.
Nevertheless, weakness remains beneath the market’s surface: tariffs, inflation, soaring energy prices and rising borrowing costs have all put pressure on equities.

Ameriprise chief market strategist Anthony Saglimbene said, “Market breadth has actually deteriorated even as the index inches toward a new high.” He is referring to the shrinking proportion of stocks that are joining the rally.

Saglimbene noted that while AI‑related stocks have regained favor, utility shares are lagging and non‑essential consumer stocks – including auto parts, textiles and luxury‑related equities – are under pressure, with “many stocks far below their 52‑week highs.”

S&P nears new high but over half its components are down more than 20% Even as the S&P 500 closes in on the August peak, Dow Jones data show that 59.2% of its constituents are at least 20% below their historic highs.

Many on Wall Street treat a drop of 20% or more from a historic high as the definition of a bear market. Yet many heavily‑hit S&P 500 stocks have been extremely volatile lately and could swing 20% or more within a few months.

Dow Jones data indicate that, at least since the end of 2017, the S&P 500 has never been within 1% of its all‑time high while simultaneously having such a high share of components down more than 20% from their own peaks. This is the first time this has happened since the bullish run that began in October 2022.
Some investors see this as a sign of underlying risk, while others argue it shows the market’s resilience.

Franklin Templeton Institute senior market strategist Chris Galipeau said most people might think “things are getting out of control,” citing soaring gasoline and diesel prices, the Iran war, and doubts about the Fed’s credibility in hitting a 2% inflation target.

Galipeau added that U.S. economic and corporate earnings resilience in the first six months of the year has exceeded expectations, “this story is hard to refute” unless the Fed ultimately raises rates sharply enough to drag down growth.

Oil prices and high yields remain market worries Nonetheless, the Iran conflict, the 10‑year U.S. Treasury yield hovering near 5%, and the Fed’s renewed anti‑inflation stance are shaping investors’ asset‑allocation decisions.
U.S. gasoline is now around $4.50 per gallon and diesel has hit a record $6.50 per gallon, while living‑cost and borrowing pressures continue to rise.
Even if the Fed hikes rates once or a few times, it is unlikely to halt hyperscalers from continuing massive AI investments.

Kevin Gordon, head of macro‑economic research and strategy at Schwab’s research center, said, “It’s been a massive capital‑rotation process. To me, that’s the essence of this year’s market. You’ll see some sectors and groups weaken for a spell, but not all sectors will falter together.”
Global benchmark Brent crude has risen about 25% over the past three months, returning to $100 a barrel and intensifying cost‑of‑living crises for many households.

Nevertheless, many energy stocks in the S&P 500 are still trading near historic highs, including Marathon Petroleum (MPC‑US), Valero Energy (VLO‑US) and Phillips 66 (PSX‑US). All three closed in the red on Monday, slipping 4‑5%.
Gordon described the market’s current state as a “cautious climb over a wall of concern.”

items.title: 158萬人都在做！勞退自提6%真的划算嗎？
items.title_en: 158 Million People Are Doing It! Is a 6% Voluntary Labor Pension Contribution Really Worth It?
paras: 做勞退自提的人，真的愈來愈多了
根據勞保局截至2026年7月底統計，勞退提繳總人數約786.6萬人，其中自願提繳已超過158.3萬人，自提率首度突破兩成、來到20.13%。換句話說，現在每5名勞工，就有1人每個月主動從薪水裡多存一筆退休金。
更值得注意的是，自提人數比2025年底增加約22.2萬人，短短7個月成長16.29%。50歲以上勞工自提比例更達32.38%，接近每3人就有1人自提，就連29歲以下的年輕勞工參與人數也持續增加。
退休準備，已經不是50歲以後再來想的事
看到愈來愈多人自提，是不是代表每個人都適合來做勞退自提呢？答案不一定。因為自提6%不是單純的多存一點錢，而是拿現在的現金流，交換未來的退休資產。值不值得，還得看你的收入、稅率、現金需求，以及這幾年有沒有買房、結婚、生育或創業等計畫。
先搞懂公司的6%，不是從你薪水扣的
很多人聽到勞退6%，第一個反應都是「公司不是已經幫我扣了嗎？」其實不一樣。在勞退新制下，雇主依法必須按月提繳不低於勞工工資6%的退休金，存進勞工個人專戶，這筆錢是公司另外負擔，不會從你的薪水裡扣。
而我們常說的「勞退自提」，則是勞工自己決定，再從薪資中額外提撥，最高可以到6%。也就是說，如果雇主提6%、自己也提6%，每個月等於有相當於提繳工資12%的金額進入退休金專戶。
假設勞退月提繳工資為5萬元，雇主每月提繳3,000元，如果自己再自提6%，薪水會另外扣3,000元。最後每個月共有6,000元進入退休金專戶。
但要注意，前面的3,000元本來就有，真正影響你每月可用薪水的，是自己多提的那3,000元。所以真正該問的不是「6%好不好」，而是應該確認你自己現在少拿這3,000元，對生活有沒有影響？
為什麼愈來愈多人願意自提？3個原因最直接
好處一：強迫存錢
很多人不是收入不夠，而是薪水一增加，生活支出也跟著升級。原本告訴自己每個月要投資5,000元，最後常常變成月底剩多少再說。而勞退自提剛好反過來，在你薪水進帳以前就直接先扣掉，等於先替未來的自己留下一筆錢，再用剩下的安排生活。對總是「想存但存不到」的人來說，這反而是它最大的優點。
好處二：錢開始幫你工作
自提的退休金，會和雇主提繳的退休金一起進入個人專戶，參與勞退基金運用，投資收益也會累積回自己的帳戶。而且勞退制度設有最低收益保障。依規定，等到勞工依法請領退休金時，如果整段提繳期間的累積收益低於依當地銀行兩年期定期存款利率計算的最低收益，差額由國庫補足。
不過這裡有一個很容易被誤會的地方。ㄩ有最低收益保障，不代表勞退基金每一年都不會虧錢。基金單年度仍可能隨著市場上上下下，真正受到保障的是請領時的「累積最低收益」，所以不能直接把過去的投資績效當成未來每年的保證報酬率。
好處三：存退休金還可以少繳一點稅

勞工在每月工資6%範圍內自願提繳的退休金，不計入當年度薪資所得課稅，這是不少中高所得族群開始注意勞退自提的原因。簡單來說，原本要拿來繳所得稅的一部分薪資，可以先進退休金專戶。因此所得愈高、適用的所得稅率愈高，自提帶來的當年度節稅效果通常也會愈明顯。但不是看到年薪多少，就能直接算出省多少稅。實際稅額仍會受到免稅額、各項扣除額、家庭申報方式與其他所得影響。所以對有些人來說，節稅很有感，對另外一些人，自提真正的價值反而是在強迫儲蓄。
聽起來很好？先別急，自提也有3個代價
代價一：當這筆錢投進去之後，不是想拿就能拿
一般情況下，必須符合勞退退休金請領條件後才能領取。這也是自提與自己買ETF、基金或放銀行最大的不同。
假設你這幾年正準備買房，需要100萬元頭期款；或準備結婚、生小孩、創業，甚至工作收入可能中斷，那麼眼前的現金可能比退休帳戶多幾萬元更重要。退休固然重要，但如果為了多存退休金，臨時需要錢時反而得刷卡循環、借信貸，就本末倒置了。
代價二：這筆錢不能自己決定怎麼投資
自己投資，可以選台股、美股、ETF、債券，甚至隨著年齡調整資產配置。勞退自提沒有這個選項。資金會交由勞動基金統一運用，勞工無法自行指定要買股票、債券或哪一檔ETF。對沒時間研究投資、不想每天看盤的人來說，這反而很省事。
但如果本身已有完整投資規劃，也願意承受市場波動來換取長期成長機會，就必須考慮要不要把所有能存下來的錢，都鎖進不能自行配置的退休帳戶。
代價三：不是每個人節稅都很有感
如果扣除免稅額與各項扣除額後，本來就幾乎不需要繳所得稅，自提帶來的直接節稅效果自然有限。而這時候還要不要自提？就要回到另外兩個理由：你需不需要強迫儲蓄，以及是否希望替退休多累積一筆不容易被挪用的資金。節稅是優點，但不是所有人自提6%的唯一理由。
那到底誰比較適合直接自提6%？
可以先問自己4個問題。有沒有準備至少6至12個月的緊急預備金？目前有沒有信用卡循環或其他高利率負債？未來幾年有沒有買房、結婚、生育或創業等大筆資金需求？現在每個月少6%的薪資，生活還能不能維持原本的品質？
如果緊急預備金已經準備好、沒有高利率負債、短期沒有大額用錢需求，而且目前所得適用較高的所得稅率，那麼自提6%的財效益通常會比較明顯。
尤其是距離退休愈來愈近、但退休準備仍明顯不足的人，自提也能成為加速累積退休資產的方法之一。這也是為什麼目前50歲以上勞工的自提比例最高。
年輕人不一定一開始就要衝6%
剛出社會的人可能會遇到薪水才剛開始增加，一邊租房、一邊存緊急預備金，還想準備未來的買房頭期款。這時候如果每個月硬把6%全部鎖進退休帳戶，反而可能讓現在的財務彈性變得很低。
其實自提不是0或6%的二選一，如果現金流還沒有那麼寬裕，可以先從1%、2%或3%開始，等到未來加薪、預備金補足，或短期財務目標完成，再慢慢往上調整，也是一種做法。
退休準備，不能只靠一個6%
勞退自提很像替未來的自己，設了一個不能隨便打開的存錢筒。它的優點是有紀律、可以長期累積，也可能帶來節稅效果。缺點則是流動性低，而且不能自己決定如何投資。
所以退休規劃真正該做的，不是把所有錢都塞進同一個地方。比較完整的方式，可以把資金分成三層：
第一層，是隨時能拿出來的緊急預備金與短期生活需求。
第二層，是透過勞退自提，替退休保留一筆不容易被挪用的長期資產。
第三層，才是股票、ETF、基金或其他可以自主配置的投資，兼顧長期成長與資金彈性。
自提6%，是退休規劃的起點
勞退自提率首度突破20%，代表愈來愈多人開始把退休規劃變成現在每個月真的在做的事。而它最大的價值，在於透過固定提撥，把退休準備真正落實在每一個月，而不是等到接近退休時，才開始擔心資金是否足夠。
對現金流穩定、短期沒有重大資金需求的人來說，善用自提，不只是多存一筆退休金，也是在替未來建立一筆不容易被挪用的長期資產。但當退休準備開始累積後，下一步就不能只看勞退帳戶裡有多少錢。
手上的現金、股票、ETF、基金、保險、房地產，甚至未來的退休現金流，都需要一起放進來看，才能知道目前的資產配置，是否真的足以提供給我們未來想要的生活。

paras_en: People who make voluntary labor pension contributions are truly increasing in number.

According to the Labor Insurance Bureau’s statistics as of the end of July 2026, about 7.866 million workers have contributed to the labor pension, of which over 1.583 million have done so voluntarily, pushing the voluntary contribution rate past 20% for the first time, reaching 20.13%. In other words, now one out of every five workers actively sets aside an extra retirement fund from their salary each month.

Even more noteworthy, the number of voluntary contributors grew by about 222,000 since the end of 2025, a 16.29% increase in just seven months. Workers over 50 have a voluntary contribution rate of 32.38%, almost one in three, and participation among workers under 29 continues to rise as well.
Retirement preparation is no longer something to think about only after turning 50.

Seeing more people contribute voluntarily doesn’t necessarily mean it’s right for everyone. Voluntary 6% isn’t just saving a little extra; it’s swapping current cash flow for future retirement assets. Whether it’s worthwhile depends on your income, tax rate, cash needs, and whether you have plans such as buying a house, marriage, children, or starting a business in the coming years.
First, understand the company’s 6% – it’s not deducted from your salary.

Many hear “6% labor pension” and immediately think, “Isn’t the company already deducting that for me?” It’s actually different. Under the new labor pension system, employers are legally required to contribute at least 6% of an employee’s wages each month into a personal pension account, and this amount is borne by the company, not taken from your paycheck.

What we call “voluntary labor pension contribution” is when the employee decides to allocate an additional amount from their salary, up to a maximum of 6%. So if the employer contributes 6% and the employee also contributes 6%, the total amount entering the pension account each month equals 12% of the wage.

For example, if the monthly pension contribution base is NT$50,000, the employer contributes NT$3,000 each month. If the employee adds a voluntary 6%, another NT$3,000 is deducted from the salary, resulting in a total of NT$6,000 going into the pension account each month.

However, note that the original NT$3,000 from the employer is already there; the only amount that actually reduces your take‑home pay is the extra NT$3,000 you choose to contribute. Therefore, the real question isn’t “Is 6% good?” but rather whether losing that NT$3,000 each month impacts your current lifestyle.
Why are more and more people willing to contribute voluntarily? Three direct reasons:
Benefit 1: Forced saving.

Many people don’t lack income; when their salary rises, their living expenses rise too. They might plan to invest NT$5,000 each month, but often end up spending whatever is left at month‑end. Voluntary pension contributions work the opposite way: the money is deducted before the salary hits your account, effectively reserving a sum for your future self, and you live on the remainder. For those who always “want to save but can’t,” this is the biggest advantage.
Benefit 2: Your money starts working for you.

The voluntarily contributed pension, together with the employer’s contribution, goes into a personal account that participates in the labor pension fund’s investments, and the investment returns accrue to your account. Moreover, the system guarantees a minimum return. By law, when a worker legally claims the pension, if the cumulative return over the contribution period is lower than the minimum calculated based on the two‑year term deposit rate of local banks, the shortfall is covered by the treasury.

But there’s a common misunderstanding: having a minimum‑return guarantee does not mean the fund never loses money in a given year. The fund can still fluctuate with the market; the guarantee applies only to the “cumulative minimum return” at the time of withdrawal, so past performance can’t be taken as a guaranteed annual rate.
Benefit 3: Contributing to the pension can also reduce your tax bill slightly.

Voluntary contributions up to 6% of monthly wages are excluded from taxable salary income for that year, which is why many middle‑ and high‑income earners pay attention to voluntary pension contributions. Simply put, a portion of salary that would otherwise be subject to income tax can be redirected into the pension account. The higher your income and marginal tax rate, the more noticeable the tax‑saving effect. However, you can’t calculate the exact tax saved just from annual salary; actual tax payable also depends on exemptions, deductions, filing status, and other income. Hence, for some people the tax benefit feels significant, while for others the real value lies in forced saving.
Sounds good? Hold on – there are three costs to consider.
Cost 1: Once the money is invested, you can’t just take it out whenever you want.

Generally, you can only withdraw the pension after meeting the retirement eligibility conditions. This is the biggest difference between voluntary contributions and buying ETFs, mutual funds, or keeping cash in a bank.

Imagine you’re saving for a NT$1 million down‑payment on a house, or planning marriage, children, a startup, or even facing a possible income interruption. In such cases, having a few extra tens of thousands of cash on hand may be more important than the retirement account. Retirement is important, but if you lock away money for it and then have to rely on credit cards or loans for short‑term needs, you’ve got it backwards.
Cost 2: You can’t decide how the money is invested.

When you invest on your own, you can choose Taiwanese stocks, U.S. stocks, ETFs, bonds, and adjust asset allocation as you age. Voluntary labor pension contributions don’t offer that choice. The funds are managed centrally by the labor pension fund, and employees cannot specify which stocks, bonds, or ETFs to buy. For those who lack time to research or don’t want to monitor the market daily, this can actually be convenient.

But if you already have a comprehensive investment plan and are willing to tolerate market volatility for long‑term growth, you need to consider whether locking all your savable cash into a non‑customizable retirement account makes sense.
Cost 3: Not everyone feels a strong tax‑saving benefit.

If, after exemptions and deductions, you barely owe any income tax, the direct tax‑saving effect of voluntary contributions is naturally limited. In that case, the decision to contribute should revert to the other two reasons: do you need forced saving, and do you want to build a retirement fund that’s hard to divert? Tax savings are a plus, but not the sole reason for a 6% contribution.
So who is actually best suited for a straight 6% voluntary contribution?

Start by asking yourself four questions: Do you have an emergency fund covering at least 6–12 months? Do you have any high‑interest credit‑card debt or other costly liabilities? Will you need large sums for a house, marriage, children, or a startup in the next few years? Can you maintain your current lifestyle with a 6% reduction in monthly salary?

If you have a solid emergency fund, no high‑interest debt, no imminent large‑cash needs, and your current income is taxed at a relatively high marginal rate, the financial benefit of a 6% contribution is usually more evident.

Especially for those approaching retirement but still lacking sufficient preparation, a voluntary contribution can accelerate the accumulation of retirement assets – which explains why workers over 50 have the highest contribution rates.
Young people don’t necessarily need to jump straight to 6%.

Recent graduates may see their salary rise modestly while juggling rent, building an emergency fund, and saving for a future house down‑payment. Locking the full 6% into a retirement account right away could severely limit their short‑term financial flexibility.

In fact, voluntary contribution isn’t an all‑or‑nothing choice between 0% and 6%. If cash flow is tight, you can start with 1%, 2% or 3%, and increase the rate as you get raises, build up your emergency fund, or achieve short‑term goals.
Retirement preparation can’t rely on a single 6% contribution.

Voluntary labor pension contributions are like a piggy bank you can’t easily open for your future self. Their strengths are discipline, long‑term accumulation, and possible tax benefits. Their weaknesses are low liquidity and lack of investment control.
Therefore, a proper retirement plan shouldn’t dump all money into one place. A more complete approach divides assets into three layers:
The first layer is an emergency fund and short‑term living‑expense cash that you can access at any time.
The second layer is the retirement fund built through voluntary labor pension contributions – a long‑term asset that’s hard to divert.
The third layer consists of stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, or other investments you can allocate yourself, balancing long‑term growth with liquidity.
A 6% contribution is just the starting point of retirement planning.

The labor pension voluntary contribution rate breaking the 20% mark shows that more people are turning retirement planning into a monthly habit. Its greatest value lies in turning a fixed monthly allocation into concrete retirement preparation, rather than waiting until retirement to worry about whether you have enough money.

For those with stable cash flow and no major short‑term financial needs, using voluntary contributions not only adds to retirement savings but also creates a long‑term asset that’s difficult to misuse. However, once your retirement savings start to grow, the next step isn’t just looking at the pension balance.

You need to consider cash, stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, insurance, real estate, and future retirement cash flow together to see whether your overall asset allocation truly supports the lifestyle you want in the future.

items.title: 馬斯克聯手輝達押注軌道AI！100萬顆衛星上限已申請  太空機房要比星鏈大百倍
items.title_en: Musk Teams with Nvidia to Bet on Orbital AI! 1 Million Satellite Cap Already Applied, Space Data Centers to Be Hundreds of Times Larger Than Starlink
paras: 矽谷知名投資人、巴倫資本創辦人Ron Baron上周四(17日)在面向客戶的投資人大會上，系統地推廣馬斯克旗下軌道AI專案「Starmind(星智)」。
Baron把太空資料中心的成本邏輯概括為：地面資料中心是「10美元資本投入加每年2美元維護運作」，太空則是「一次性2美元」；衛星每5年換一代、效能提升10倍，10年內容量可翻100倍，未來每年能湊出100GW電力。不過，這些數據均來自Baron個人表述，而非第三方審計結論。
監理端與工程端的進展則是有據可查。美國聯邦通訊委員會(FCC)今年2月4日發佈公開通知，接受SpaceX的軌道資料中心系統申請並徵求公眾意見。
文件顯示，SpaceX今年1月30日申請在500至2000公里高度的近地軌道部署最多100萬顆衛星，運行於30度及太陽同步軌道傾角，主要依靠星間光鏈路互聯，並可連接第一代、第二代星鏈衛星。同時，SpaceX在申請中請求豁免NGSO部署進度節點、保證金等義務，並要求免於按處理輪次申請18.3—19.3GHz及28.6—29.1GHz頻段。
需要區分的是，100萬顆是向FCC申請的系統規模上限，不等於實際部署量。星鏈當年申請4.2萬顆、實際在軌約1萬顆，申請規模預留未來餘裕為航太業慣例。
賓州大學教授Benjamin C. Lee先前公開表示，目前全球在軌衛星合計約1.5萬顆。此外，申請文件未揭露衛星尺寸、重量、具體軌道參數、部署時間表與成本預估，技術細節缺失仍是監管與產業界的核心質疑。
與輝達的合作關係已由官方確認。輝達上月24日宣布，SpaceXAI計畫將加速運算能力延伸至太空，第一代Starmind AI衛星將基於優化後的輝達Vera Rubin NVL72機架級系統構建，雙方正共同適配軌道運算在供電、熱管理、頻寬、可靠性與物理整合上的約束。
SpaceX在財報電話會議上指出，未來所有AI算力將獨家採用輝達架構，首顆AI衛星計畫於今年第四季發射，2028年達到顯著規模
成本與資本開支是爭議最集中的環節。伍德麥肯錫(Wood Mackenzie)在報告中估算，一個假設性的1GW軌道資料中心造價約1700億美元，是地面同等設施的3倍以上，其中發射與衛星成本約佔總成本的60%，但要將軌道成本降至與地面持平，需實現70%的成本降幅。
伍德麥肯錫基準情境甚至未納入大規模軌道資料中心，明確指出其目前仍是「對成本曲線的押注」。
資本開支方面，摩根士丹利分析師Adam Jonas預估，SpaceX 2026年AI相關資本支出約530億美元，2027年約1300億美元，折合每瓦約40美元。支援方認為，軌道資料中心可規避地面設施的監管障礙與社區阻力，星艦推動的發射成本下降將持續改善經濟性。
但批評人士指出，昂貴的AI晶片與高昂的發射成本仍是現實門檻，現階段經濟模型尚未跑通。
另有投行給予較樂觀的長線判斷，認為SpaceX到2031年底可部署約75GW軌道算力，成本顯著低於地面建設，可望成為其發射與星鏈業務以外的新營收來源。
paras_en: Silicon Valley investor and Baren Capital founder Ron Baron promoted Elon Musk’s orbital AI project “Starmind” to clients at a conference on Thursday, the 17th.

Baron summarized the cost logic of space data centers as: a ground data center costs $10 in capital plus $2 per year in operating expenses, while space costs a one‑time $2; satellites are refreshed every five years with ten‑fold performance gains, yielding a hundred‑fold increase in capacity over ten years and the ability to generate 100 GW of power annually. These figures come from Baron’s own statements, not third‑party audits.

Regulatory and engineering progress can be verified. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) issued a public notice on February 4, accepting SpaceX’s orbital data‑center system application and seeking public comment.

The filing shows SpaceX applied on Jan 30 to deploy up to 1 million satellites in low‑Earth orbit at 500‑2,000 km, operating at 30° and sun‑synchronous inclinations, primarily linked via inter‑satellite optical links and compatible with first‑ and second‑generation Starlink satellites. SpaceX also requested waivers for NGSO deployment milestones, security deposits and exemption from filing for the 18.3‑19.3 GHz and 28.6‑29.1 GHz bands on a per‑round basis.

It should be noted that the 1 million figure is the maximum system size requested from the FCC, not the actual deployment count. Starlink originally applied for 42,000 satellites but has about 10,000 in orbit, a common practice of reserving future capacity in the aerospace industry.

University of Pennsylvania professor Benjamin C. Lee has previously stated that roughly 15,000 satellites are currently in orbit worldwide. The application does not disclose satellite size, mass, exact orbital parameters, deployment schedule or cost estimates, leaving technical details a core concern for regulators and the industry.

The partnership with Nvidia has been confirmed by officials. Nvidia announced on the 24th of last month that the SpaceX AI project will extend compute power to space, with the first‑generation Starmind AI satellites built on an optimized Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 rack‑level system, and both parties are jointly adapting orbital computing to constraints in power, thermal management, bandwidth, reliability and physical integration.

SpaceX said in its earnings call that all future AI compute will exclusively use Nvidia architecture, with the first AI satellite slated for launch in Q4 this year and a significant scale expected by 2028.

Cost and capital expenditure are the most contentious issues. Wood Mackenzie estimated in a report that a hypothetical 1 GW orbital data center would cost about $170 billion, more than three times the cost of an equivalent ground facility, with launch and satellite costs accounting for roughly 60 % of total cost; a 70 % cost reduction would be needed to bring orbital costs in line with ground‑based ones.
Wood Mackenzie’s baseline scenario does not even include a large‑scale orbital data center, explicitly stating that it remains a bet on the cost curve.

On the cap‑ex side, Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas projects SpaceX’s AI‑related capital spending at about $53 billion in 2026 and $130 billion in 2027, roughly $40 per watt. Proponents argue that orbital data centers avoid ground‑based regulatory hurdles and community opposition, and that the cost reductions from Starship launches will continue to improve economics.
Critics counter that expensive AI chips and high launch costs remain real barriers, and that the economic model is not yet proven.

Some investment banks are more optimistic long‑term, estimating SpaceX could have roughly 75 GW of orbital compute capacity deployed by the end of 2031, at costs significantly lower than ground construction, potentially becoming a new revenue stream beyond its launch and Starlink businesses.

items.title: 比爾蓋茲警告：AI就像人造外星人 不能再當普通科技看待
items.title_en: Bill Gates Warns: AI Is Like Man‑Made Aliens, No Longer a Ordinary Technology
paras: 比爾蓋茲近日表示，人工智慧（AI）與過往所有技術都不一樣，若僅將其視為既有科技的延續，恐怕容易掉以輕心。他更將AI發展比喻為「外星人降臨」，強調這些「外星人」不是搭乘太空船而來，而是由人類親手創造，並被置入電腦之中。
蓋茲在紐約出席基金會目標守衛者會議時指出，他原本希望自己只需要談論對外援助，以及如何降低兒童死亡率，但AI快速發展，使他在與各國領導人會面時，不得不同時討論另一項迫切問題：社會是否已為這場變革做好準備，以及如何面對技術可能帶來的風險。
AI進展之快，約在一年前便讓蓋茲感到震驚。他指出，AI如今已能完成程式設計工作，而這項技能是他年輕時花費大量時間才得以掌握。
AI不僅可以編寫程式碼，也能研究程式碼、找出漏洞，甚至可能被用來入侵各類系統，展現出的能力已超越單純提升效率的工具。
不過，真正令蓋茲擔憂的並非只有技術本身，而是社會尚未對AI的指數級進步展開足夠廣泛的參與和討論。
科技業內部雖已開始探討相關風險，但更廣泛的大眾仍未充分投入，社會對這項技術的理解與準備，明顯落後於AI演進速度。
蓋茲形容，當前的改變就像「十本科幻小說裡的情節同時發生」。傳統科幻作品通常只圍繞一項重大技術突破展開，但AI可能同時推動多個領域快速變革，因此不能再以過往看待單一科技創新的方式加以理解。
他強調，AI極為特殊，人類未來將走向何方，取決於如何對待這項技術。因應AI挑戰的第一步，是讓更多人參與其中，不僅成為技術的使用者，也要了解背後潛藏的風險，避免AI議題只停留在科技產業內部。
蓋茲也提醒，AI具有明顯的兩面性。一方面，它可望在農業與公共衛生領域推動創新；另一方面，也可能帶來難以忽視的安全風險。如何合理運用AI、同時建立對風險的認識，將成為社會必須共同面對的課題。
談及全球發展時，蓋茲對部分富裕國家削減對低收入國家的援助表示遺憾。他指出，在經濟持續成長、企業獲利屢創新高之際，許多富裕國家的政府卻變得更加吝嗇。
他並非要求世界的一部分拯救另一部分，而是主張透過慷慨投入推動共同進步，協助資源匱乏、仍努力挽救生命的社區。
蓋茲呼籲恢復資金支持，以保障最基本的生存需求。他認為，若能將更多公益投入與AI的合理運用相結合，便有機會加快實現全球公平的目標。
paras_en: Bill Gates recently said that artificial intelligence (AI) is unlike any technology before; treating it merely as a continuation of existing tech could lead to complacency. He likened AI development to “aliens arriving,” emphasizing that these “aliens” aren’t coming in spaceships but are created by humans and embedded in computers.

Speaking at the Foundation’s Guardians of the Goal conference in New York, Gates noted that he originally hoped to talk only about foreign aid and how to reduce child mortality, but the rapid advance of AI forced him, when meeting world leaders, to also discuss a pressing issue: whether society is ready for this transformation and how to confront the risks the technology may bring.
The speed of AI progress shocked Gates about a year ago. He pointed out that AI can now perform programming tasks—a skill he spent a great deal of time mastering when he was younger.
AI can not only write code but also analyze it, find vulnerabilities, and could even be used to breach various systems, showing capabilities that go beyond being a simple efficiency‑boosting tool.
However, what truly worries Gates is not just the technology itself but the fact that society has not engaged broadly enough in discussion about AI’s exponential advancement.

While the tech industry has begun to explore related risks, the wider public remains insufficiently involved; society’s understanding and preparation for this technology lag clearly behind the pace of AI’s evolution.

Gates described the current change as “ten sci‑fi novel plots happening at once.” Traditional sci‑fi usually focuses on a single breakthrough, but AI may drive rapid transformation across multiple fields simultaneously, so it can no longer be understood through the lens of past single‑technology innovations.

He stressed that AI is exceptionally unique, and humanity’s future direction depends on how we treat it. The first step in meeting AI’s challenges is to involve more people—not just as users of the technology but also as aware of its hidden risks—to prevent AI discussions from staying confined to the tech industry.

Gates also warned that AI has a clear dual nature. On one hand, it promises innovation in agriculture and public health; on the other, it poses significant security risks. Balancing sensible AI use with risk awareness will become a societal issue that must be tackled together.

When speaking about global development, Gates expressed regret over some wealthy nations cutting aid to low‑income countries. He noted that while economies keep growing and corporate profits hit record highs, many rich‑country governments are becoming more stingy.
He is not calling for one part of the world to rescue another, but advocates generous investment to drive shared progress, helping resource‑poor communities that are still striving to save lives.

Gates urged the restoration of funding to secure basic survival needs. He believes that if more philanthropy is combined with responsible AI deployment, there is an opportunity to accelerate the achievement of global equity.

items.title: 地緣政治緊張推升原油期貨 Meta AI熱潮助攻亞洲股市
items.title_en: Geopolitical Tensions Lift Crude Oil Futures, Meta AI Hype Boosts Asian Stocks
paras: 地緣政治情勢發展與人工智慧(AI)需求增溫，同時成為周二(22日)影響國際原油價格與亞洲股市走勢的主因。

美伊會談前景不明

受市場對本周聯合國大會期間美伊會談的樂觀情緒減退影響，國際原油期貨價格周二走高。根據洲際交易所(ICE)數據，近月布蘭特原油期貨上漲 1.6%，收在每桶 101.99 美元；近月西德州中級原油(WTI)期貨上揚 1.7%，收在每桶 97.40 美元。
各國領袖本周齊聚位於紐約的聯合國大會，美國總統川普與伊朗總統裴澤斯基安(Masoud Pezeshkian)均預定發表演說，川普還計畫於紐約期間與多位中東領袖會面。
多位外交官指出，卡達官員擬利用此次大會場合，討論重啟美伊對話的可能性。不過外交圈與市場普遍認為，由於大會期間尚未確認會舉行正式的美伊雙邊會談，因此出現重大突破的機會不高。

Meta AI代理引發關注

在科技股與大盤表現方面，亞股周二普遍上揚。台灣加權指數在IC與半導體類股領漲帶動下，盤中一度創下歷史新高，最終收盤上漲 0.2%。南韓綜合股價指數(Kospi)早盤走高後回吐部分漲幅，終場收升 0.25%。
此波股市漲勢主要來自市場對晶片需求的樂觀情緒增強。美國科技巨頭 Meta Platforms 推出的全新 AI 代理(AI agent)引發市場高度關注，進一步激勵全球 AI 概念股表現。其中，晶片製造龍頭 SK 海力士與三星電子占據南韓 Kospi 指數約 50% 的市值，成為撐盤的主要動能。
日股仍處連假期間，將繼續休市至周三。
paras_en: Geopolitical developments and rising demand for artificial intelligence (AI) were the main drivers on Tuesday the 22nd of international crude oil prices and Asian equity market movements.

Uncertainty over a US‑Iran dialogue. With optimism fading about a possible US‑Iran talks during this week’s United Nations General Assembly, international crude oil futures rose on Tuesday. According to Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) data, the near‑month Brent crude futures gained 1.6% to $101.99 a barrel, while the near‑month West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures climbed 1.7% to $97.40 a barrel.

World leaders gathered this week at the UN General Assembly in New York, where US President Donald Trump and Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian are scheduled to deliver speeches, and Trump also plans to meet several Middle‑East leaders while in New York.

Several diplomats said Qatari officials intend to use the assembly as a venue to discuss the possibility of restarting US‑Iran talks. However, both diplomatic circles and the market generally believe that, since no formal bilateral US‑Iran meeting has been confirmed for the summit, the chance of a breakthrough is low.

Meta AI agent draws attention. In terms of tech stocks and broader market performance, Asian equities rose overall on Tuesday. items.title: 鉅亨投資雷達》高所得族群必看！投資海外如何用境內基金聰明節稅？
items.title_en: Jiheng Investment Radar: A Must‑Read for High‑Income Earners! How to Smartly Save Taxes on Overseas Investments Using Domestic Funds
paras: 高所得族群常透過境外基金、海外ETF或海外帳戶配置美股、科技股與全球股票，以分散單一市場風險。但當海外所得達100萬元、基本所得額超過750萬元時，境外投資獲利就可能產生額外稅負。究竟同樣投資於海外股市的境內外基金稅額有何差異？為什麼境內基金能夠節稅？
1. 境外基金屬海外所得，可能產生額外稅負
由下表可以看到，若投資人海外所得未達100萬元，便無需考量額外稅負問題。若單一申報戶之海外所得達100萬元，則其海外所得須全數計入基本所得額；但只有當基本所得額超過750萬元時，超過部分會才會產生基本稅額。
海外投資是否產生額外稅負由海外所得金額及基本所得額決定
但並非所有達成條件之投資人皆須繳納這筆基本稅額，應觀察計算得出之基本稅額是否高於一般所得稅額。（所得適用稅率請參考：配息族看這裡！會計師教你如何少繳稅）以同樣海外所得達100萬元、基本所得額超過750萬元之投資人為例：（假設稅率/免稅額/扣除額採115年度、兩人皆單身無撫養、採單身標準扣除額，且無海外已納稅額扣抵）

林先生的年薪資收入為350萬元，扣除免稅額、標準扣除額、薪資所得特別扣除額，綜合所得淨額為303.6萬元，一般所得稅額為48.07萬元。若其海外所得為600萬元，因超過100萬元須全數計入基本所得額，為903.6萬元，則基本稅額= (903.6萬-750萬) × 20%= 30.72萬元。因基本稅額小於一般所得稅額，因此無須補繳稅。
王小姐年薪資收入同樣為350萬元，其綜合所得淨額亦為303.6萬元、一般所得稅額48.07萬元。若其海外所得為800萬元，則其基本稅額= (1,103.6萬-750萬) × 20%= 70.72萬元。因基本稅額超過一般所得稅額，王小姐須補繳70.72萬-48.07萬=22.65萬元。


（更多「最低稅負制」相關說明請參考：
2026海外所得多少不用繳稅？750萬以下要申報嗎？免稅額試算一次看）
2. 投資要考量稅務，但分散配置仍有必要

投資人可能會想：「既然海外所得可能產生額外稅負，我不要投資海外不就好了？」但這樣反而會讓投資組合承擔更高的風險。以產業配置來看，台股基金高度集中於資訊科技產業，占比高達74%，遠高於美股基金的42%與環球股票基金的37%；相較之下，美國與環球股票基金在工業、金融、非必須消費、醫療保健等產業的分布更平均。換言之，只投資台股雖然看似避開海外所得課稅問題，卻可能讓資產過度押注單一市場、單一產業與單一貨幣。
因此，高所得族群配置海外資產仍有其必要性。第一，能夠分散台股集中在半導體與科技供應鏈的風險；第二，可以參與全球不同產業與區域的成長機會；第三，也能降低資產過度集中於新台幣與台灣市場的曝險。真正的重點不是因為稅務考量而放棄海外投資，而是透過更有效率的稅務與基金持有架構，把海外曝險納入整體財富規劃中，兼顧成長、分散與稅負管理。
3. 為什麼高所得族群應選擇境內基金？
同樣投資海外，境內外基金稅負有所不同
那麼到底該怎麼做，才能在投資海外股市的同時，減少可能因海外所得產生的額外稅負？最簡單的方式就是選擇境內基金！從下表可以看到，同樣是投資海外市場，基金註冊地不同，投資人面對的稅務結果可能不同：以台灣投資人來說，透過境內基金投資海外股債，若報酬主要來自基金淨值上漲，投資人贖回時的資本利得（價差）免稅；但若直接投資境外基金，贖回獲利、配息等多屬海外所得，須依最低稅負制規則檢視。
同樣投資海外，境內基金可能產生之稅額更低
選擇境內基金能省去稅務計算之麻煩

假設一對夫妻各有國內年薪300萬元，兩人合計薪資收入為600萬元。依115年度免稅額、標準扣除額與薪資所得特別扣除額計算，扣除後綜合所得淨額為507.2萬元。若夫妻薪資所得採分開計稅、合併報繳，依115年度綜合所得稅率試算，兩人合計一般所得稅額為70.82 萬元。由前段已知，海外投資的額外稅負繳納條件為：同一申報戶海外所得超過100萬元、納入海外所得之基本所得額超過750萬元，且基本稅額超過一般所得稅額。依上述條件試算，這對夫妻的海外所得補稅門檻為596.9萬元；也就是海外所得超過此水準後，便會產生需補繳之稅額。
麻煩的是，若投資人長期累積境外基金，直到退休才一次贖回，高額資本利得可能在單一年度推高基本所得額，進而產生巨大補稅壓力；若選擇在退休前分批贖回，也需每年重新檢視國內所得及一般所得稅額，並重新計算海外所得補稅門檻，再進行多次申購、贖回以精準控制當年度海外所得金額。相較之下，若透過境內基金配置海外股市，因其資本利得免稅的特性，可降低投資人在實現海外資產獲利時面臨最低稅負制的複雜度。
4. 境內也有許多績效優異的美股/科技/全球股票基金！
境內投資於海外股市、表現好的基金有哪些？
投資海外股市的境內基金中，仍有不少績效遠優於同類平均。以美股、全球科技及全球股票基金來看，這些境內基金不只今年以來報酬明顯領先，拉長至1年、2年與3年期也持續優於同類平均，顯示投資人即使選擇境內基金，仍有機會參與海外市場成長，同時兼顧稅務效率與資產配置分散。
如何在「鉅亨買基金」找到這些基金？
投資人可進入「鉅亨買基金」網站，點選「找基金」中的「基金搜尋」，再依序篩選基金註冊地與基金類型。例如，若想尋找境內海外股票基金，可先選擇「境內」，接著依投資需求篩選「全球股票」、「美國股票」或「資訊科技股票」等類別。
若資訊科技股票類別中同時包含台股科技基金與海外科技基金，投資人可進一步點開基金持股明細，確認主要投資市場與前十大持股，判斷是否真正布局海外股票。此外，也可從基金代號來辨識註冊地：以「鉅亨買基金」平台販售基金為例，代號以A開頭為境內基金，以B開頭則為境外基金，可搭配基金頁面資訊交叉確認。

海外資產仍是高所得族群分散配置的重要工具。對需要特別留意海外所得及稅務規劃的投資人而言，境內基金可作為參與海外市場時兼顧配置與稅務效率的優先選擇。

paras_en: High‑income earners often allocate U.S. stocks, tech stocks and global equities through offshore funds, overseas ETFs or foreign accounts to diversify away from a single market risk. However, when overseas income reaches NT$1 million and total taxable income exceeds NT$7.5 million, profits from foreign investments may trigger additional tax liabilities. What is the tax difference between domestic and offshore funds that both invest in overseas equities? Why can domestic funds provide tax savings?
1. Overseas funds are classified as foreign‑source income and may generate extra tax liabilities

The table below shows that if an investor’s foreign‑source income is below NT$1 million, no additional tax needs to be considered. If a single‑taxpayer’s foreign income reaches NT$1 million, the entire amount must be included in the basic taxable income; only the portion that pushes the basic taxable income above NT$7.5 million will be subject to the basic tax.
Whether overseas investment creates extra tax depends on the amount of foreign income and the level of basic taxable income

However, not every investor who meets the thresholds must actually pay the basic tax. One must compare the calculated basic tax with the regular income tax. (For applicable tax rates, see: “Dividend‑receivers, look here! Accountants teach you how to reduce tax”). For illustration, consider investors with foreign income of NT$1 million and basic taxable income over NT$7.5 million (assuming 2015 tax rates, both single, no dependents, using the standard deduction, and no foreign tax credits).

Mr. Lin’s annual salary is NT$3.5 million. After subtracting the exemption, standard deduction and special salary deduction, his net comprehensive income is NT$3.036 million, yielding a regular income tax of NT$480,700. If his foreign income is NT$6 million, because it exceeds NT$1 million it must be fully added to basic income, resulting in NT$9.036 million. The basic tax = (NT$9.036 million – NT$7.5 million) × 20% = NT$307,200. Since the basic tax is lower than the regular tax, no additional tax is due. Ms. Wang also earns a salary of NT$3.5 million, with the same net comprehensive income of NT$3.036 million and regular tax of NT$480,700. If her foreign income is NT$8 million, the basic tax = (NT$11.036 million – NT$7.5 million) × 20% = NT$707,200. Because this exceeds the regular tax, Ms. Wang must pay an extra NT$226,500 (NT$707,200 – NT$480,700).
(For more details on the “minimum tax” system, see: “How much overseas income in 2026 is tax‑free? Do you need to file if it’s under NT$7.5 million? Quick exemption calculation”)
2. Tax considerations are important, but diversification remains necessary

Investors might think: “If overseas income can cause extra tax, why not avoid overseas investments altogether?” Doing so would actually increase portfolio risk. In terms of sector allocation, Taiwan‑stock funds are heavily weighted toward information technology (about 74%), far higher than U.S. equity funds (42%) and global equity funds (37%). By contrast, U.S. and global funds have a more balanced exposure to industrials, financials, consumer discretionary, healthcare and other sectors. In other words, investing only in Taiwan stocks may appear to sidestep foreign‑income tax, but it can over‑concentrate assets in a single market, industry and currency.

Therefore, high‑income earners still need overseas assets. First, it diversifies away from the concentration of Taiwanese stocks in semiconductors and the tech supply chain. Second, it provides exposure to growth opportunities across different industries and regions worldwide. Third, it reduces over‑exposure to the New Taiwan dollar and the domestic market. The key is not to abandon overseas investments because of tax, but to incorporate them into an overall wealth plan through more tax‑efficient structures, balancing growth, diversification and tax management.
3. Why should high‑income earners choose domestic funds?
The tax burden differs between domestic and offshore funds even when both invest abroad

So how can investors reduce the extra tax that may arise from foreign‑source income while still investing in overseas equities? The simplest way is to use domestic funds. The table below shows that, although both types invest in foreign markets, the tax outcome varies with the fund’s registration location: for Taiwanese investors, capital gains (price appreciation) from domestic funds that invest in overseas stocks and bonds are tax‑free when redeemed, whereas gains and dividends from directly holding offshore funds are treated as foreign income and must be examined under the minimum‑tax rules.
Domestic funds investing abroad may result in lower tax liabilities
Choosing domestic funds also eliminates the hassle of tax calculations

Assume a married couple each earns a domestic salary of NT$3 million, for a combined salary of NT$6 million. Using 2015 exemption, standard deduction and special salary deduction, their net comprehensive income is NT$5.072 million. If they file separately or jointly, the combined regular income tax (based on 2015 rates) is NT$708,200. From the earlier discussion, the condition for extra foreign‑income tax is: a single tax unit’s foreign income exceeds NT$1 million, the resulting basic taxable income exceeds NT$7.5 million, and the basic tax exceeds the regular tax. Applying these criteria, the couple’s foreign‑income surcharge threshold is NT$5.969 million; only when foreign income surpasses this level will additional tax be required.

The problem arises if investors accumulate offshore funds over many years and redeem everything at retirement. A large capital gain in one year could push basic taxable income high enough to trigger a substantial surcharge. By contrast, using domestic funds to gain exposure to overseas equities benefits from tax‑free capital gains, reducing the complexity of the minimum‑tax system when realizing foreign‑asset profits.

Among domestic funds that invest abroad, many outperform their peers. In U.S., global tech and global equity categories, these funds have not only led in returns year‑to‑date, but also continue to beat peer averages over 1‑, 2‑ and 3‑year horizons, showing that investors can still capture overseas market growth while enjoying tax efficiency and diversified asset allocation.

items.title: 隱形冠軍又少一個？台灣扣件市占穩居全球前三 「斷崖式」人力缺口年增24%成隱憂
items.title_en: Another Invisible Champion Lost? Taiwan's Fastener Market Share Remains in Global Top Three, “Cliff‑like” Labor Shortage Grows 24% Year‑over‑Year as a Hidden Concern
paras: 台灣為全球第3大扣件出口地區，近年來扣件產業「高值化」轉型逐步顯現成效。根據扣件業者統計，2026年8月單月出口總額達3.57億美元，雖受到全球建材及一般工業需求放緩影響，年減6.93％，但今年前8月平均出口單價逆勢上揚5.15％，攀升至每公斤3.67美元，顯示台灣業者轉型高附加價值產品的策略已展現成果。但也受到少子化、缺工潮衝擊，今年的扣件產業職缺即呈現大幅度年增高達24.53％。
目前市面上的扣件產品包含螺絲、螺帽、扣環與墊圈等，廣泛應用於航太、電動車與醫療等高階領域。據美國知名媒體報導，台灣扣件產量約占全球13％，長年穩居全球主要出口國；產業資料亦顯示，台灣為全球第3大扣件出口地區，逾9成產品外銷。其中美國為第1大市場，出口額達17億9420萬美元，占比達42.7％。
隨著AI與資料中心建設推進，半導體先進製程、封測及AI伺服器供應鏈擴產，帶動高科技製造設備對具備耐腐蝕、耐高溫與高精度特性的「高階扣件」需求增加，推升產業對專業技術人才的需求。
1111人力銀行統計顯示，扣件產業相關工作機會數較去年同期成長24.53％。部分主管職缺月薪7萬起跳，獎金另計，凸顯具備專業技術與管理經驗的人才極具價值。
不過，產業也正面臨技術人才斷層問題。臺灣螺絲工業同業公會理事長蔡永裕表示，目前扣件業缺工嚴重，技術熟練的師傅多集中在40至65歲，一旦資深人員退休，恐影響產線運作與技術延續。
1111人力銀行發言人莊雨潔建議，面對高齡化與技術斷層，企業應建構製程SOP、案例資料庫，甚至導入AI協助整理技術邏輯，將經驗轉化為資產。轉職者亦可聚焦AI與自動化轉型，運用數位工具強化履歷與面試表現，搶進傳產高薪職缺。
paras_en: Taiwan is the world’s third‑largest fastener export region, and the industry’s shift toward higher‑value products is gradually bearing fruit. According to fastener manufacturers, total exports in August 2026 reached US$357 million for the month; although global construction‑material and general‑industrial demand slowed, causing a 6.93% year‑over‑year decline, the average export price for the first eight months of the year rose 5.15% against the trend to US$3.67 per kilogram, showing that Taiwan’s strategy of moving to higher‑added‑value products is paying off. However, the industry is also hit by low birth rates and a labor shortage, with fastener‑related job openings increasing sharply by 24.53% year‑over‑year.

Current fastener products on the market include screws, nuts, rings and washers, which are widely used in high‑end sectors such as aerospace, electric vehicles and medical devices. According to a well‑known U.S. media outlet, Taiwan’s fastener output accounts for about 13% of global production, maintaining a long‑standing position among the world’s major exporters; industry data also show that Taiwan is the third‑largest fastener export region, with over 90% of its products sold abroad. The United States is the top market, with export value reaching US$1.7942 billion, representing 42.7% of total exports.

As AI and data‑center construction advance, and the semiconductor advanced‑process, packaging and AI‑server supply chains expand, demand for “high‑end fasteners” that offer corrosion resistance, high‑temperature tolerance and high precision is increasing, driving up the need for specialized technical talent in the industry.

Statistics from 1111 Job Bank show that the number of job opportunities in the fastener sector grew 24.53% compared with the same period last year. Some supervisory positions start at a monthly salary of NT$70,000, with bonuses paid separately, highlighting the high value of talent with professional technical and management experience.

Nevertheless, the industry is facing a technical talent gap. Cai Yong‑yu, chairman of the Taiwan Screw Industry Association, said the fastener sector is suffering a severe labor shortage, with skilled craftsmen concentrated in the 40‑to‑65‑year‑old age group; once these senior workers retire, production lines and technology transfer could be jeopardized.

Zhuang Yujie, spokesperson for 1111 Job Bank, recommends that, in the face of an aging workforce and skill gap, companies should establish process SOPs and case databases, and even introduce AI to help organize technical logic, turning experience into assets. Career‑switchers can focus on AI and automation transformation, using digital tools to strengthen their resumes and interview performance to secure high‑salary positions in traditional manufacturing.

items.title: 針對涉嫌違反伊朗制裁 美聯邦檢察官調查幣安
items.title_en: US Federal Prosecutors Investigate Binance Over Alleged Iran Sanctions Violations
paras: 美國紐約曼哈頓聯邦檢察官正針對全球最大加密貨幣交易所幣安(Binance)展開調查，釐清平台是否涉及違反美國對伊朗的經濟制裁規定。
此前，美國司法部已針對涉嫌經由兩家香港公司(Blessed Trust 與 Hexa Whale)透過幣安洗錢的 6,100 萬美元伊朗黑市石油收益提出民事沒收訴訟，儘管檢方在訴訟中未直接指控幣安存在不當行為，仍使幣安再度面臨美國聯邦機構的監管審查。
針對本次調查與先前的合規質疑，幣安發言人Ross O'Leary發表書面聲明強調：「我們對違反制裁行為採取零容忍政策。我們全力配合執法機關，並持續致力於根除與停權不良行為者。」
針對媒體報導合規人員因舉報違規交易遭解雇一事，幣安官方於部落格澄清離職與調查無關，並表示：「無論是加密貨幣或傳統金融交易所，都無法保證風險絕不觸及平台。負責任機構的差別在於風險發生時能否加以偵測、調查、化解並通報，而幣安在所有案例中皆已做到這四點。」
近年美方持續加大對伊朗的經濟封鎖，據區塊鏈分析機構 Chainalysis 估計，2025 年流入受制裁實體的加密貨幣金額暴增近 700%，高達 1,040 億美元。媒體如《華爾街日報》與《紐約時報》曾指出，幣安內部曾有調查員針對十餘億美元涉伊朗交易提出疑慮。
由於聯邦檢察官啟動調查並不等同於正式起訴，刑事調查也可能在未發布指控的情況下結案。目前美國司法部與曼哈頓檢察官辦公室發言人均拒絕發表評論。
paras_en: U.S. federal prosecutors in Manhattan are launching an investigation into Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, to determine whether the platform was involved in violations of U.S. economic sanctions against Iran.

Previously, the U.S. Department of Justice filed a civil forfeiture lawsuit seeking to seize $61 million of Iranian black‑market oil proceeds that were allegedly laundered through Binance via two Hong Kong companies, Blessed Trust and Hexa Whale. Although the complaint did not directly accuse Binance of wrongdoing, it has again placed the exchange under scrutiny by U.S. federal regulators.

In response to the investigation and earlier compliance concerns, Binance spokesperson Ross O’Leary issued a written statement emphasizing, “We have a zero‑tolerance policy for sanctions violations. We are fully cooperating with law‑enforcement authorities and remain committed to rooting out and disabling bad actors.”

Addressing media reports that a compliance employee was fired after reporting illicit trades, Binance clarified on its blog that the departure was unrelated to any investigation and said, “Whether in crypto or traditional finance, no exchange can guarantee that risk will never touch the platform. The difference for a responsible institution is whether it can detect, investigate, mitigate and report when risk materializes, and Binance has done all four in every case.”

In recent years the United States has intensified its economic blockade of Iran. Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis estimates that crypto flowing to sanctioned entities will surge by nearly 700% by 2025, reaching $104 billion. Media outlets such as the Wall Street Journal and the New York Times have reported that Binance internal investigators raised concerns over more than $10 billion in Iran‑related transactions.

Because the launch of a federal investigation does not equate to formal charges, a criminal probe can be closed without any indictment. Both the Department of Justice and the Manhattan U.S. Attorney’s Office declined to comment at this time.

items.title_en: Materials-KY (4763) Spends NT$11.7B to Acquire Global Top‑3 Peer Cerdia! Expands Footprint Across Four Continents, Merger Benefits Depend on Three Variables
paras: 2026年09月22日（優分析／產業數據中心報導）⸺ 材料*-KY(4763-TW)昨(21)日晚間召開重大訊息記者會，宣布將以現金加股票方式，取得全球醋酸纖維絲束大廠Cerdia Holding的100%股權，交易總金額約3.68億美元，折合新台幣約117億元，成為公司近年規模最大的一筆跨國併購案。
公司預計支付約2.14億美元現金，折合新台幣約68億元，並增發約9.95%普通股支付其餘對價，代表公司將同時承擔大額現金支出與流通股本擴張，因此，後續除了觀察併購帶來的營收成長，也要留意每股獲利的稀釋程度，如果併購後營收、產能利用率快速反映，新增獲利才有機會抵銷股本膨脹。
Cerdia擁有逾百年纖維材料製造經驗，員工約1,100人，為全球前三大醋酸纖維絲束製造商之一，並在歐洲、美洲設有生產與研發據點。交易完成後，材料*-KY(4763-TW)的營運版圖將由目前以中國生產基地為主，進一步延伸至亞洲、歐洲、北美洲及南美洲。

從中國單一基地走向跨洲供應，客戶結構也將改變
材料*-KY(4763-TW)過去主要依靠中國生產基地供應全球市場，競爭優勢來自製造效率、成本控管及上下游垂直整合；Cerdia加入後，集團將形成兩套互補的供應系統。
Cerdia將以醋酸纖維絲束為主要產品，並服務歐美大型客戶；材料*-KY(4763-TW)則持續發展紡織材料、眼鏡框、手機殼及車用電池等原材料。雙方不僅產品應用可以互補，既有客戶的重疊程度也相對有限，使這筆併購不只是增加產能，更有機會直接擴大客戶及區域市場。
交易完成後，材料*-KY(4763)將由原本較集中的中國製造模式，轉向橫跨四大洲的在地生產與供應體系，面對關稅、物流及地緣政治變化時，可提高原料調度與交貨彈性，也能縮短與歐美客戶之間的供應距離。
這筆交易讓材料*-KY(4763-TW)一次補上歐洲與美洲生產布局，但規模擴大不等於獲利立即增加。後續除了觀察主管機關核准與交割進度，更重要的是Cerdia能否帶來足以抵銷現金支出、整合成本及近一成股權稀釋的獲利與現金流，這才是併購案能否真正提升股東價值的關鍵。

paras_en: September 22, 2026 (U-Analysis/Industry Data Center report) – Materials‑KY (4763‑TW) held a major news conference last night (the 21st) and announced that it will acquire 100% of Cerdia Holding, a world‑leading producer of acetate filament bundles, in a cash‑and‑stock deal valued at about US$368 million, or roughly NT$11.7 billion, making it the company’s largest cross‑border acquisition in recent years.

The company plans to pay about US$214 million in cash (approximately NT$6.8 billion) and issue roughly 9.95% of its common shares for the remaining consideration, meaning it will incur a sizable cash outlay and a dilution of its share capital. Consequently, investors will need to watch not only revenue growth from the deal but also the degree of earnings per share dilution; only if post‑merger revenue and capacity utilization rise quickly can the added profit offset the expanded equity base.

Cerdia brings over a century of fiber‑material manufacturing experience, about 1,100 employees, and is one of the top three global producers of acetate filament bundles, with production and R&D sites in Europe and the Americas. After the transaction closes, Materials‑KY’s operational map will expand from its current China‑centric base to include Asia, Europe, North America and South America.

Moving from a single China base to a multi‑continent supply network will also change the customer mix. Materials‑KY has traditionally relied on its Chinese manufacturing hub to serve the global market, leveraging manufacturing efficiency, cost control and vertical integration; with Cerdia added, the group will operate two complementary supply systems.

Cerdia will focus on acetate filament bundles for large European and American customers, while Materials‑KY will continue developing raw materials for textiles, eyewear frames, mobile‑phone cases and automotive batteries. The product lines are complementary and the overlap of existing customers is limited, so the acquisition not only adds capacity but also offers a direct route to expand the customer base and regional markets.

After the deal, Materials‑KY will shift from a relatively concentrated China‑manufacturing model to a localized production and supply system spanning four continents. This broader footprint can improve raw‑material scheduling and delivery flexibility amid tariff, logistics and geopolitical shifts, and shorten supply distances to European and American clients.

The transaction gives Materials‑KY an immediate production presence in Europe and the Americas, but a larger scale does not automatically translate into higher profits. Beyond regulatory approval and closing milestones, the key question is whether Cerdia can generate enough profit and cash flow to offset the cash outlay, integration costs and roughly ten‑percent equity dilution, which will determine if the deal truly enhances shareholder value.

根據勞保局截至2026年7月底統計，勞退提繳總人數約786.6萬人，其中自願提繳已超過158.3萬人，自提率首度突破兩成、來到20.13%。換句話說，現在每5名勞工，就有1人每個月主動從薪水裡多存一筆退休金。
更值得注意的是，自提人數比2025年底增加約22.2萬人，短短7個月成長16.29%。50歲以上勞工自提比例更達32.38%，接近每3人就有1人自提，就連29歲以下的年輕勞工參與人數也持續增加。
退休準備，已經不是50歲以後再來想的事
看到愈來愈多人自提，是不是代表每個人都適合來做勞退自提呢？答案不一定。因為自提6%不是單純的多存一點錢，而是拿現在的現金流，交換未來的退休資產。值不值得，還得看你的收入、稅率、現金需求，以及這幾年有沒有買房、結婚、生育或創業等計畫。
先搞懂公司的6%，不是從你薪水扣的
很多人聽到勞退6%，第一個反應都是「公司不是已經幫我扣了嗎？」其實不一樣。在勞退新制下，雇主依法必須按月提繳不低於勞工工資6%的退休金，存進勞工個人專戶，這筆錢是公司另外負擔，不會從你的薪水裡扣。
而我們常說的「勞退自提」，則是勞工自己決定，再從薪資中額外提撥，最高可以到6%。也就是說，如果雇主提6%、自己也提6%，每個月等於有相當於提繳工資12%的金額進入退休金專戶。
假設勞退月提繳工資為5萬元，雇主每月提繳3,000元，如果自己再自提6%，薪水會另外扣3,000元。最後每個月共有6,000元進入退休金專戶。
但要注意，前面的3,000元本來就有，真正影響你每月可用薪水的，是自己多提的那3,000元。所以真正該問的不是「6%好不好」，而是應該確認你自己現在少拿這3,000元，對生活有沒有影響？
為什麼愈來愈多人願意自提？3個原因最直接
好處一：強迫存錢
很多人不是收入不夠，而是薪水一增加，生活支出也跟著升級。原本告訴自己每個月要投資5,000元，最後常常變成月底剩多少再說。而勞退自提剛好反過來，在你薪水進帳以前就直接先扣掉，等於先替未來的自己留下一筆錢，再用剩下的安排生活。對總是「想存但存不到」的人來說，這反而是它最大的優點。
好處二：錢開始幫你工作
自提的退休金，會和雇主提繳的退休金一起進入個人專戶，參與勞退基金運用，投資收益也會累積回自己的帳戶。而且勞退制度設有最低收益保障。依規定，等到勞工依法請領退休金時，如果整段提繳期間的累積收益低於依當地銀行兩年期定期存款利率計算的最低收益，差額由國庫補足。
不過這裡有一個很容易被誤會的地方。ㄩ有最低收益保障，不代表勞退基金每一年都不會虧錢。基金單年度仍可能隨著市場上上下下，真正受到保障的是請領時的「累積最低收益」，所以不能直接把過去的投資績效當成未來每年的保證報酬率。
好處三：存退休金還可以少繳一點稅

勞工在每月工資6%範圍內自願提繳的退休金，不計入當年度薪資所得課稅，這是不少中高所得族群開始注意勞退自提的原因。簡單來說，原本要拿來繳所得稅的一部分薪資，可以先進退休金專戶。因此所得愈高、適用的所得稅率愈高，自提帶來的當年度節稅效果通常也會愈明顯。但不是看到年薪多少，就能直接算出省多少稅。實際稅額仍會受到免稅額、各項扣除額、家庭申報方式與其他所得影響。所以對有些人來說，節稅很有感，對另外一些人，自提真正的價值反而是在強迫儲蓄。
聽起來很好？先別急，自提也有3個代價
代價一：當這筆錢投進去之後，不是想拿就能拿
一般情況下，必須符合勞退退休金請領條件後才能領取。這也是自提與自己買ETF、基金或放銀行最大的不同。
假設你這幾年正準備買房，需要100萬元頭期款；或準備結婚、生小孩、創業，甚至工作收入可能中斷，那麼眼前的現金可能比退休帳戶多幾萬元更重要。退休固然重要，但如果為了多存退休金，臨時需要錢時反而得刷卡循環、借信貸，就本末倒置了。
代價二：這筆錢不能自己決定怎麼投資
自己投資，可以選台股、美股、ETF、債券，甚至隨著年齡調整資產配置。勞退自提沒有這個選項。資金會交由勞動基金統一運用，勞工無法自行指定要買股票、債券或哪一檔ETF。對沒時間研究投資、不想每天看盤的人來說，這反而很省事。
但如果本身已有完整投資規劃，也願意承受市場波動來換取長期成長機會，就必須考慮要不要把所有能存下來的錢，都鎖進不能自行配置的退休帳戶。
代價三：不是每個人節稅都很有感
如果扣除免稅額與各項扣除額後，本來就幾乎不需要繳所得稅，自提帶來的直接節稅效果自然有限。而這時候還要不要自提？就要回到另外兩個理由：你需不需要強迫儲蓄，以及是否希望替退休多累積一筆不容易被挪用的資金。節稅是優點，但不是所有人自提6%的唯一理由。
那到底誰比較適合直接自提6%？
可以先問自己4個問題。有沒有準備至少6至12個月的緊急預備金？目前有沒有信用卡循環或其他高利率負債？未來幾年有沒有買房、結婚、生育或創業等大筆資金需求？現在每個月少6%的薪資，生活還能不能維持原本的品質？
如果緊急預備金已經準備好、沒有高利率負債、短期沒有大額用錢需求，而且目前所得適用較高的所得稅率，那麼自提6%的財效益通常會比較明顯。
尤其是距離退休愈來愈近、但退休準備仍明顯不足的人，自提也能成為加速累積退休資產的方法之一。這也是為什麼目前50歲以上勞工的自提比例最高。
年輕人不一定一開始就要衝6%
剛出社會的人可能會遇到薪水才剛開始增加，一邊租房、一邊存緊急預備金，還想準備未來的買房頭期款。這時候如果每個月硬把6%全部鎖進退休帳戶，反而可能讓現在的財務彈性變得很低。
其實自提不是0或6%的二選一，如果現金流還沒有那麼寬裕，可以先從1%、2%或3%開始，等到未來加薪、預備金補足，或短期財務目標完成，再慢慢往上調整，也是一種做法。
退休準備，不能只靠一個6%
勞退自提很像替未來的自己，設了一個不能隨便打開的存錢筒。它的優點是有紀律、可以長期累積，也可能帶來節稅效果。缺點則是流動性低，而且不能自己決定如何投資。
所以退休規劃真正該做的，不是把所有錢都塞進同一個地方。比較完整的方式，可以把資金分成三層：
第一層，是隨時能拿出來的緊急預備金與短期生活需求。
第二層，是透過勞退自提，替退休保留一筆不容易被挪用的長期資產。
第三層，才是股票、ETF、基金或其他可以自主配置的投資，兼顧長期成長與資金彈性。
自提6%，是退休規劃的起點
勞退自提率首度突破20%，代表愈來愈多人開始把退休規劃變成現在每個月真的在做的事。而它最大的價值，在於透過固定提撥，把退休準備真正落實在每一個月，而不是等到接近退休時，才開始擔心資金是否足夠。
對現金流穩定、短期沒有重大資金需求的人來說，善用自提，不只是多存一筆退休金，也是在替未來建立一筆不容易被挪用的長期資產。但當退休準備開始累積後，下一步就不能只看勞退帳戶裡有多少錢。
手上的現金、股票、ETF、基金、保險、房地產，甚至未來的退休現金流，都需要一起放進來看，才能知道目前的資產配置，是否真的足以提供給我們未來想要的生活。

paras_en: People who make voluntary labor pension contributions are truly increasing in number.

According to the Labor Insurance Bureau’s statistics as of the end of July 2026, about 7.866 million workers have contributed to the labor pension, of which over 1.583 million have done so voluntarily, pushing the voluntary contribution rate past 20% for the first time, reaching 20.13%. In other words, now one out of every five workers actively sets aside an extra retirement fund from their salary each month.

Even more noteworthy, the number of voluntary contributors grew by about 222,000 since the end of 2025, a 16.29% increase in just seven months. Workers over 50 have a voluntary contribution rate of 32.38%, almost one in three, and participation among workers under 29 continues to rise as well.
Retirement preparation is no longer something to think about only after turning 50.

Seeing more people contribute voluntarily doesn’t necessarily mean it’s right for everyone. Voluntary 6% isn’t just saving a little extra; it’s swapping current cash flow for future retirement assets. Whether it’s worthwhile depends on your income, tax rate, cash needs, and whether you have plans such as buying a house, marriage, children, or starting a business in the coming years.
First, understand the company’s 6% – it’s not deducted from your salary.

Many hear “6% labor pension” and immediately think, “Isn’t the company already deducting that for me?” It’s actually different. Under the new labor pension system, employers are legally required to contribute at least 6% of an employee’s wages each month into a personal pension account, and this amount is borne by the company, not taken from your paycheck.

What we call “voluntary labor pension contribution” is when the employee decides to allocate an additional amount from their salary, up to a maximum of 6%. So if the employer contributes 6% and the employee also contributes 6%, the total amount entering the pension account each month equals 12% of the wage.

For example, if the monthly pension contribution base is NT$50,000, the employer contributes NT$3,000 each month. If the employee adds a voluntary 6%, another NT$3,000 is deducted from the salary, resulting in a total of NT$6,000 going into the pension account each month.

However, note that the original NT$3,000 from the employer is already there; the only amount that actually reduces your take‑home pay is the extra NT$3,000 you choose to contribute. Therefore, the real question isn’t “Is 6% good?” but rather whether losing that NT$3,000 each month impacts your current lifestyle.
Why are more and more people willing to contribute voluntarily? Three direct reasons:
Benefit 1: Forced saving.

Many people don’t lack income; when their salary rises, their living expenses rise too. They might plan to invest NT$5,000 each month, but often end up spending whatever is left at month‑end. Voluntary pension contributions work the opposite way: the money is deducted before the salary hits your account, effectively reserving a sum for your future self, and you live on the remainder. For those who always “want to save but can’t,” this is the biggest advantage.
Benefit 2: Your money starts working for you.

The voluntarily contributed pension, together with the employer’s contribution, goes into a personal account that participates in the labor pension fund’s investments, and the investment returns accrue to your account. Moreover, the system guarantees a minimum return. By law, when a worker legally claims the pension, if the cumulative return over the contribution period is lower than the minimum calculated based on the two‑year term deposit rate of local banks, the shortfall is covered by the treasury.

But there’s a common misunderstanding: having a minimum‑return guarantee does not mean the fund never loses money in a given year. The fund can still fluctuate with the market; the guarantee applies only to the “cumulative minimum return” at the time of withdrawal, so past performance can’t be taken as a guaranteed annual rate.
Benefit 3: Contributing to the pension can also reduce your tax bill slightly.

Voluntary contributions up to 6% of monthly wages are excluded from taxable salary income for that year, which is why many middle‑ and high‑income earners pay attention to voluntary pension contributions. Simply put, a portion of salary that would otherwise be subject to income tax can be redirected into the pension account. The higher your income and marginal tax rate, the more noticeable the tax‑saving effect. However, you can’t calculate the exact tax saved just from annual salary; actual tax payable also depends on exemptions, deductions, filing status, and other income. Hence, for some people the tax benefit feels significant, while for others the real value lies in forced saving.
Sounds good? Hold on – there are three costs to consider.
Cost 1: Once the money is invested, you can’t just take it out whenever you want.

Generally, you can only withdraw the pension after meeting the retirement eligibility conditions. This is the biggest difference between voluntary contributions and buying ETFs, mutual funds, or keeping cash in a bank.

Imagine you’re saving for a NT$1 million down‑payment on a house, or planning marriage, children, a startup, or even facing a possible income interruption. In such cases, having a few extra tens of thousands of cash on hand may be more important than the retirement account. Retirement is important, but if you lock away money for it and then have to rely on credit cards or loans for short‑term needs, you’ve got it backwards.
Cost 2: You can’t decide how the money is invested.

When you invest on your own, you can choose Taiwanese stocks, U.S. stocks, ETFs, bonds, and adjust asset allocation as you age. Voluntary labor pension contributions don’t offer that choice. The funds are managed centrally by the labor pension fund, and employees cannot specify which stocks, bonds, or ETFs to buy. For those who lack time to research or don’t want to monitor the market daily, this can actually be convenient.

But if you already have a comprehensive investment plan and are willing to tolerate market volatility for long‑term growth, you need to consider whether locking all your savable cash into a non‑customizable retirement account makes sense.
Cost 3: Not everyone feels a strong tax‑saving benefit.

If, after exemptions and deductions, you barely owe any income tax, the direct tax‑saving effect of voluntary contributions is naturally limited. In that case, the decision to contribute should revert to the other two reasons: do you need forced saving, and do you want to build a retirement fund that’s hard to divert? Tax savings are a plus, but not the sole reason for a 6% contribution.
So who is actually best suited for a straight 6% voluntary contribution?

Start by asking yourself four questions: Do you have an emergency fund covering at least 6–12 months? Do you have any high‑interest credit‑card debt or other costly liabilities? Will you need large sums for a house, marriage, children, or a startup in the next few years? Can you maintain your current lifestyle with a 6% reduction in monthly salary?

If you have a solid emergency fund, no high‑interest debt, no imminent large‑cash needs, and your current income is taxed at a relatively high marginal rate, the financial benefit of a 6% contribution is usually more evident.

Especially for those approaching retirement but still lacking sufficient preparation, a voluntary contribution can accelerate the accumulation of retirement assets – which explains why workers over 50 have the highest contribution rates.
Young people don’t necessarily need to jump straight to 6%.

Recent graduates may see their salary rise modestly while juggling rent, building an emergency fund, and saving for a future house down‑payment. Locking the full 6% into a retirement account right away could severely limit their short‑term financial flexibility.

In fact, voluntary contribution isn’t an all‑or‑nothing choice between 0% and 6%. If cash flow is tight, you can start with 1%, 2% or 3%, and increase the rate as you get raises, build up your emergency fund, or achieve short‑term goals.
Retirement preparation can’t rely on a single 6% contribution.

Voluntary labor pension contributions are like a piggy bank you can’t easily open for your future self. Their strengths are discipline, long‑term accumulation, and possible tax benefits. Their weaknesses are low liquidity and lack of investment control.
Therefore, a proper retirement plan shouldn’t dump all money into one place. A more complete approach divides assets into three layers:
The first layer is an emergency fund and short‑term living‑expense cash that you can access at any time.
The second layer is the retirement fund built through voluntary labor pension contributions – a long‑term asset that’s hard to divert.
The third layer consists of stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, or other investments you can allocate yourself, balancing long‑term growth with liquidity.
A 6% contribution is just the starting point of retirement planning.

The labor pension voluntary contribution rate breaking the 20% mark shows that more people are turning retirement planning into a monthly habit. Its greatest value lies in turning a fixed monthly allocation into concrete retirement preparation, rather than waiting until retirement to worry about whether you have enough money.

For those with stable cash flow and no major short‑term financial needs, using voluntary contributions not only adds to retirement savings but also creates a long‑term asset that’s difficult to misuse. However, once your retirement savings start to grow, the next step isn’t just looking at the pension balance.

You need to consider cash, stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, insurance, real estate, and future retirement cash flow together to see whether your overall asset allocation truly supports the lifestyle you want in the future.

paras: 台灣為全球第3大扣件出口地區，近年來扣件產業「高值化」轉型逐步顯現成效。根據扣件業者統計，2026年8月單月出口總額達3.57億美元，雖受到全球建材及一般工業需求放緩影響，年減6.93％，但今年前8月平均出口單價逆勢上揚5.15％，攀升至每公斤3.67美元，顯示台灣業者轉型高附加價值產品的策略已展現成果。但也受到少子化、缺工潮衝擊，今年的扣件產業職缺即呈現大幅度年增高達24.53％。
目前市面上的扣件產品包含螺絲、螺帽、扣環與墊圈等，廣泛應用於航太、電動車與醫療等高階領域。據美國知名媒體報導，台灣扣件產量約占全球13％，長年穩居全球主要出口國；產業資料亦顯示，台灣為全球第3大扣件出口地區，逾9成產品外銷。其中美國為第1大市場，出口額達17億9420萬美元，占比達42.7％。
隨著AI與資料中心建設推進，半導體先進製程、封測及AI伺服器供應鏈擴產，帶動高科技製造設備對具備耐腐蝕、耐高溫與高精度特性的「高階扣件」需求增加，推升產業對專業技術人才的需求。
1111人力銀行統計顯示，扣件產業相關工作機會數較去年同期成長24.53％。部分主管職缺月薪7萬起跳，獎金另計，凸顯具備專業技術與管理經驗的人才極具價值。
不過，產業也正面臨技術人才斷層問題。臺灣螺絲工業同業公會理事長蔡永裕表示，目前扣件業缺工嚴重，技術熟練的師傅多集中在40至65歲，一旦資深人員退休，恐影響產線運作與技術延續。
1111人力銀行發言人莊雨潔建議，面對高齡化與技術斷層，企業應建構製程SOP、案例資料庫，甚至導入AI協助整理技術邏輯，將經驗轉化為資產。轉職者亦可聚焦AI與自動化轉型，運用數位工具強化履歷與面試表現，搶進傳產高薪職缺。
paras_en: Taiwan is the world’s third‑largest fastener export region, and the industry’s shift toward higher‑value products is gradually bearing fruit. According to fastener manufacturers, total exports in August 2026 reached US$357 million for the month; although global construction‑material and general‑industrial demand slowed, causing a 6.93% year‑over‑year decline, the average export price for the first eight months of the year rose 5.15% against the trend to US$3.67 per kilogram, showing that Taiwan’s strategy of moving to higher‑added‑value products is paying off. However, the industry is also hit by low birth rates and a labor shortage, with fastener‑related job openings increasing sharply by 24.53% year‑over‑year.

Current fastener products on the market include screws, nuts, rings and washers, which are widely used in high‑end sectors such as aerospace, electric vehicles and medical devices. According to a well‑known U.S. media outlet, Taiwan’s fastener output accounts for about 13% of global production, maintaining a long‑standing position among the world’s major exporters; industry data also show that Taiwan is the third‑largest fastener export region, with over 90% of its products sold abroad. The United States is the top market, with export value reaching US$1.7942 billion, representing 42.7% of total exports.

As AI and data‑center construction advance, and the semiconductor advanced‑process, packaging and AI‑server supply chains expand, demand for “high‑end fasteners” that offer corrosion resistance, high‑temperature tolerance and high precision is increasing, driving up the need for specialized technical talent in the industry.

Statistics from 1111 Job Bank show that the number of job opportunities in the fastener sector grew 24.53% compared with the same period last year. Some supervisory positions start at a monthly salary of NT$70,000, with bonuses paid separately, highlighting the high value of talent with professional technical and management experience.

Nevertheless, the industry is facing a technical talent gap. Cai Yong‑yu, chairman of the Taiwan Screw Industry Association, said the fastener sector is suffering a severe labor shortage, with skilled craftsmen concentrated in the 40‑to‑65‑year‑old age group; once these senior workers retire, production lines and technology transfer could be jeopardized.

Zhuang Yujie, spokesperson for 1111 Job Bank, recommends that, in the face of an aging workforce and skill gap, companies should establish process SOPs and case databases, and even introduce AI to help organize technical logic, turning experience into assets. Career‑switchers can focus on AI and automation transformation, using digital tools to strengthen their resumes and interview performance to secure high‑salary positions in traditional manufacturing.

items.title: CoWoS擴產推升ABF需求 載板三雄同步漲停、稼動率全面走高
items.title_en: CoWoS Expansion Boosts ABF Demand, Three Major Substrate Makers Hit Daily Limits, Utilization Rises Across the Board
paras: 2026年09月22日（優分析／產業數據中心報導）⸺ AI先進封裝擴產帶動高階ABF載板需求，載板三雄今(22)日同步攻上漲停。欣興(3037-TW)收1,120元，上漲100元、漲幅9.80%；南電(8046-TW)收1,165元，上漲105元、漲幅9.91%；景碩(3189-TW)收909元，上漲82元、漲幅9.92%。
CoWoS產能持續開出，是ABF載板需求成長的重要來源。隨GPU、ASIC與HBM封裝規模擴大，對高階ABF封裝基板的需求同步增加，市場預估2028年先進封裝總產能可成長約50%，載板廠也陸續提高產能利用率及資本支出。
欣興2026年第2季ABF載板稼動率已超過90%，BT約80%至85%、HDI/PCB約85%至90%；第3季估計各產品線稼動率均達90%以上。公司2026年資本支出也由原先340億元兩度追加至537億元，調幅高達57％，其中約80%至85%投入ABF。不過，高稼動率之外，T-Glass、Low CTE玻纖布等上游材料供應，已成為後續產能開出的重要限制因素。
南電產能利用率同樣維持高檔，BT載板自2026年第2季起滿載，ABF稼動率約85%；中國大陸PCB廠區第3季逐步滿載，其中崑山廠稼動率由第2季50%升至7月70%，第4季目標達100%。
景碩則規畫2027年將ABF載板產能擴增25%，幼獅廠月產能由約4,000萬顆提高至5,000萬顆，鎖定ASIC、高階交換器、Server CPU與AI相關需求。2027年資本支出初估160億元，高於2026年的140億元；BT載板目前稼動率約75%，預估年底升至85%。
海外同業也呈現高稼動率，三星電機Samsung Electro-Mechanics(009150-KR)今年上半年半導體封裝載板產線稼動率達89%，LG Innotek(011070-KR)達94%。隨主要載板廠稼動率提高，後續除了新增ABF產能，也需觀察T-Glass、Low CTE玻纖布等關鍵材料供應與新產能開出進度。

paras_en: September 22, 2026 (U-Analysis/Industry Data Center report) – The expansion of advanced AI packaging drives demand for high‑end ABF substrates, and the three leading substrate makers all hit their daily price limits today (22). Xinxing (3037‑TW) closed at NT$1,120, up NT$100 or 9.80%; NanDian (8046‑TW) closed at NT$1,165, up NT$105 or 9.91%; and JingShuo (3189‑TW) closed at NT$909, up NT$82 or 9.92%.

CoWoS capacity continues to come online, serving as a key source of ABF substrate demand growth. As GPU, ASIC and HBM packaging scales expand, the need for high‑end ABF packaging boards rises in tandem. The market estimates that total advanced‑packaging capacity will grow about 50% by 2028, and substrate manufacturers are progressively raising capacity utilization and capital expenditures.

Xinxing’s ABF substrate utilization in Q2 2026 already exceeded 90%, with BT around 80‑85% and HDI/PCB about 85‑90%; the company expects utilization across all product lines to be above 90% in Q3. Its 2026 capital spending was raised twice from the original NT$34 billion to NT$53.7 billion, a 57% increase, with roughly 80‑85% earmarked for ABF. However, beyond high utilization, upstream supplies such as T‑Glass and low‑CTE glass‑fiber cloth have become critical constraints for further capacity rollout.

NanDian’s capacity utilization also remains high; BT substrates have been fully booked since Q2 2026, and ABF utilization sits around 85%. In mainland‑China PCB factories, utilization is gradually reaching full capacity in Q3, with the Kunshan plant rising from 50% in Q2 to 70% in July and targeting 100% in Q4.

JingShuo plans to increase ABF substrate capacity by 25% in 2027, raising the Young Lion plant’s monthly output from roughly 40 million units to 50 million units, targeting ASICs, high‑end switches, server CPUs and AI‑related demand. Its 2027 capital expenditure is initially estimated at NT$16 billion, higher than the NT$14 billion slated for 2026; BT substrate utilization is currently about 75% and is projected to rise to 85% by year‑end.

Overseas peers also show high utilization: Samsung Electro‑Mechanics (009150‑KR) reported an 89% utilization rate for its semiconductor packaging substrate lines in the first half of this year, while LG Innotek (011070‑KR) reached 94%. As major substrate makers lift utilization, attention must turn to the supply of key materials such as T‑Glass and low‑CTE glass‑fiber cloth, as well as the pace of new capacity coming online.

items.title: 台積電供應鏈迅得將持續南下建立生產基地 將發行5億元無擔保CB籌資
items.title_en: TSMC Supply Chain's Shunde to Continue Expanding Southward with New Production Base and Issue NT$5 Billion Unsecured Convertible Bonds
paras: 台積電 (2330-TW) 供應鏈的設備廠迅得 (6438-TW)對最新營收推進一如預期，迅得8月營收也將維持在6億元以上高檔區， 8月營收6.11億元，改寫歷年同期新高，累計2026年1-8月營收48.18億元，年增11.5%。同時，迅得擬以5億元面額 無擔保可轉換公司債籌資，並在今(22)日獲金管會申報生效。
迅得的此一市場籌資案由台新證券主辦，可望在10月中旬完成募集。同時，迅得在積極擴大營運規模，迅得除投資南科友上科技1.5億元拿下23%股權之外，公司高層指出，迅得將有其他的投資案在進行中；同時，也最快在今年底、明年初在台灣南部取得土地建新廠，用以因應湧入的設備訂單生產。
迅得2026 年第二季營收 18.24 億元創新高，稅後純益1.66億元，單季獲利也超越首季的 1.45 億元，每股純益2.03元。2026年1-6月營收35.68億元，毛利率26.13%，稅後純益3.11億元，每股純益3.79元。而迅得公布最新營收資訊，迅得在2026 年 8月營收以 6.11 億元改寫歷年同期新高。
迅得營運總部也在遷入的新生廠後產能已進人滿載，將推升 2026 年獲利成長幅度攀高。迅得機械在 2026 年第二季營收 18.24 億元創新高，第四季由於安排出貨的半導體設備出貨逐步步入高峰，預估下半年營運勝過 上半年，全年營收將再較 2025 年的 64.67 億元再增 10-15%，再創新高。
迅得 2026 年上半年營收 35.68 億元，年增 11.99%，2026 下半年預估在出貨產品組合的有利因素加持下超過上半年表現 ，全年營收估成長 10-15%，而在獲利成長幅度可望以優於營收成長幅度倍數成長呈現。
迅得擁有在半導體及 PCB 設備需求雙重成長動能，同時，迅得在 PCB 設備指向高階產品廠商的需求，也與臻鼎 - KY(4958-TW) 及景碩 (3189-TW) 有大單確立，其中臻鼎 - KY 下單 10.2 億元，而景碩也在 7 億元之上。
paras_en: Shunde (6438‑TW), an equipment supplier in TSMC's (2330‑TW) supply chain, reported revenue growth as expected, with August revenue staying above the NT$600 million high‑end range at NT$611 million, setting a new record for the same month in history. Cumulative revenue for January‑August 2026 reached NT$4.818 billion, up 11.5% year‑over‑year. At the same time, Shunde plans to raise funds by issuing NT$5 billion of unsecured convertible bonds, which were approved by the Financial Supervisory Commission on the 22nd.

The financing round is being led by Taishin Securities and is expected to be completed by mid‑October. Shunde is also actively expanding its operations; in addition to investing NT$1.5 billion for a 23% stake in You‑Shang Technology in the Southern Science Park, senior management said other investment projects are underway. The company also aims to acquire land in southern Taiwan by the end of this year or early next year to build a new plant to meet the influx of equipment orders.

Shunde posted a record Q2 2026 revenue of NT$1.824 billion, with after‑tax net profit of NT$166 million, surpassing the first‑quarter profit of NT$145 million, and earnings per share of NT$2.03. For the first half of 2026, revenue reached NT$3.568 billion, with a gross margin of 26.13% and after‑tax net profit of NT$311 million, or NT$3.79 per share. The company also reported that August 2026 revenue of NT$611 million set a new historical high for the month.

Shunde's operations headquarters, now moved into the new factory, is already operating at full capacity, which is expected to boost profit growth in 2026. The company's machinery segment achieved a Q2 2026 revenue record of NT$1.824 billion, and the fourth quarter is expected to see a surge in semiconductor equipment shipments. Consequently, the second half of the year should outperform the first half, with full‑year revenue projected to increase another 10‑15% over the 2025 level of NT$6.467 billion, setting a new high.

Shunde's first‑half 2026 revenue of NT$3.568 billion grew 11.99% year‑over‑year. The second half is forecast to exceed the first half thanks to favorable product mix factors, leading to an overall annual revenue growth of 10‑15%. Profit growth is expected to outpace revenue growth, delivering a multiple‑fold increase.

Shunde benefits from dual growth drivers in semiconductor and PCB equipment demand. In the PCB segment, the company has secured large orders from high‑end product manufacturers, including KY (4958‑TW) and Jingshuo (3189‑TW). KY placed an order worth NT$1.02 billion, while Jingshuo's order exceeds NT$700 million.

items.title: 稜研科技(7812)今掛牌上市大漲！儀器毛利率逾70%仍虧損，衛星、FWA與國防三大專案成轉盈關鍵
items.title_en: Raytronic Technology (7812) Surges on Initial Public Offering! Instrument Gross Margins Exceed 70% Yet Still Losses, Satellite, FWA, and Defense Projects Key to Turning Profitable
paras: 稜研科技(7812-TW)今(22)日正式上市掛牌，公司以毫米波及相控陣列天線技術為核心，產品已銷往全球超過35個國家，並累積逾140項全球專利，應用範圍涵蓋5G/6G、衛星通訊、航太國防及車用雷達。
不過，稜研科技(7812-TW)目前仍面臨電信商延後毫米波部署、衛星及航太國防驗證期偏長等問題，營運規模尚未放大並處於累積虧損。因此，上市後真正值得追蹤的並非技術題材，而是衛星、FWA及國防專案能否由驗證、小量出貨進入量產，推動營收規模跨過損益兩平門檻。
(圖片來源：優分析產業資料庫)

儀器設備毛利率逾70%，模組成為第二成長曲線
稜研科技(7812-TW)目前主要有儀器設備與天線模組兩條產品線。儀器設備自2018年開始布局，已累積超過2,200名客戶，遍布34個以上國家，主要服務研究機構、電信研發單位及系統整合商。
公司表示，儀器設備營收可維持雙位數成長，毛利率更在70%以上，是現階段支撐營運的主要基本盤。隨全球通訊技術朝6G及FR3頻段發展，電信商、研究機構與設備業者對毫米波研發及量測需求同步增加，公司將持續擴充測試設備產品線，並深化與國際儀器大廠合作，以擴大海外客戶基礎及銷售規模。
第二條成長曲線則是毫米波陣列天線模組，公司採用CloverCell積木式架構提高不同產品間的零組件共通性，目前單元共用比例約30%至40%，可縮短客製化產品的開發時間，並透過採購規模降低成本。此外，公司結合台灣封裝、PCB及EMS供應鏈，導入AiP天線封裝技術，為後續量產預作準備。
不過，隨天線模組逐步放量，產品組合也將成為影響毛利率的關鍵：商用5G、6G及車用模組的出貨量較大，毛利率約10%至30%；衛星與國防產品雖然出貨量較小，但因單價及技術門檻較高，毛利率可達30%至50%。
公司長期目標是將整體平均毛利率維持在40%以上，因此，後續除了觀察天線模組能否順利放量，也要留意不同應用的出貨占比，以及商用模組放量後對整體毛利率的影響。
(圖片來源：優分析產業資料庫)

三項專案等待量產，驗證時程決定虧損改善速度
目前進度較明確的專案有三項
1. 衛星方面，稜研與北美數據機廠Comtech合作開發「One Modem、One Antenna」多軌衛星終端，產品已進行不同衛星系統的端對端測試，並規劃今年與EMS夥伴推進量產。
2. 5G／6G方面，公司與客戶及台灣ODM廠開發FWA無線回傳方案，目前系統整合接近完成，下一步將進入客戶端實地測試。公司看好相關市場具百萬套部署潛力，但實際訂單仍取決於測試結果及客戶建置時程。
3. 國防業務則已向中東客戶少量出貨，供前期驗證使用，通過驗證後才會進入量產布局。
換句話說，三項業務雖均已跨過早期研發階段，接下來的關鍵在於客戶驗證能否順利完成，並進一步轉入規模化出貨。
因此，稜研科技(7812-TW)上市後最重要的驗證，是衛星終端能否依計畫投入量產、FWA能否完成實地測試，以及國防專案能否由少量出貨轉為正式訂單。只要其中一項進入量產，營收成長幅度就可能高於原有雙位數水準；但在驗證期仍長、量產時間未完全確定的情況下，虧損收斂速度仍是接下來的核心觀察指標。
